correctness.rationale: For all n>=6, disjoint-path contraction gives every one-, two- and required three-edge incidence probability. Conditioning on exclusion of one edge gives the explicitly listed second moments. The n independent degree-star constraints, two inequivalent (n-3)-dimensional endpoint-contrast spaces, and internal-incidence kernel give an orthogonal decomposition of all allowed coordinates. Exact covariance actions give high=2(n-4)/(n-3)^2 twice and low=2(n-4)/((n-2)(n-3)) on the internal flow space, with no other eigenvalues. Walsh centering multiplies covariance by four; division yields the stated sharp ratio. The packaged checker independently enumerates all tours and checks Gram eigen-equations with exact Fractions for n=6,7,8,9. Finite tests corroborate but do not prove the universal claim.

value.rationale: This is a complete sharp all-order Riesz/frame classification for first-order Fourier coordinates on a canonical constrained travelling-salesperson ensemble, not an arbitrary numerical slice. A single forbidden edge breaks full permutation invariance yet causes only a two-level positive spectrum, with a non-generic exact coincidence of the symmetric and antisymmetric endpoint-contrast eigenvalues and sharp squared condition number 1+1/(n-3). This quantifies uniform robustness and near-isotropy of low-order sampling under one missing edge; it cannot be inferred from the classical affine dimension or generic frame inequalities. It gives exact extremizing sectors and scales to every n>=6.
